added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest records empty baseline_suite and after_suite, so no base or head gate log exists to derive an added-failure count from; this is not a measured zero

findings.text: blocking: the acceptance test list contradicts the live plan for the five DIII-D rows; the plan's §6 (since 0f6da4594, ancestor of the reviewed base f6827158) sets their clause set as global residual and every scaled row at or below 1e-6 with the value reached recorded, axis and X-point within one pitch of the EFIT reconstruction's nulls, and no map-fidelity clause, whereas lines 198-206 keep the global 1e-12 clause as the joint target, state that "the plan does not define an analytic-map/null comparator", require tests to report "oracle not specified" and forbid substituting EFIT, and no test id compares nulls with EFIT; an implementation built from this list would fail the five rows the plan passes and never run the EFIT-null clause the plan requires. Repair: restate the DIII-D clause set from the plan, add an EFIT-null position test id, and rebind line 23 to the current plan revision.

blocking: the per-resolution membership and moment caps (5e-7 symmetric difference per cell area, 2e-6 normalised current and first moment, identical from 132 to 2616 cells) are unattainable by every field representation the plan offers, because the analytic oracle carries the non-polynomial x^2 ln x particular term (nova/equilibrium/analytic_single_null.py:224) and the read reconstructs it from a discrete carrier with a local fit (the ring fit in nova/equilibrium/stencil_mesh.py is a six-coefficient quadratic); a probe of that fit on a Solov'ev flux gives boundary displacement per pitch of 2.7e-3 median at h/R0 0.13, falling as h^2 to 1.3e-4 at h/R0 0.028, three to four orders above 5e-7 at every rung (fit-probe.log in the review run). The caps borrow a clip-quadrature precedent for an error the document says includes field reconstruction (line 88), and equal caps across a twentyfold change in cell count ignore convergence order. Repair: derive resolution-dependent caps from a measured convergence study of the chosen representation on both analytic states, or separate a clip-only cap at the analytic field from a reconstruction cap that scales with pitch.

follow-on: the compensating unknowns a are Newton variables in F(psi, a) but gs.apply(psi, operands) exposes only psi as its differentiated argument, with a entering through external flux inside operands (line 96); the signature should name how a is differentiated so the augmented JVP is unambiguous.

follow-on: the private-flux row quotes the 550-cell analytic-membership sup 0.0153 but not its X-point offset 16.9 mm, which is larger than the 132-cell 5.9 mm and bears on the claim that membership alone is necessary but not sufficient.
